title: Problem Recognition
body:
Step one of [[Software Requirements Analysis]]: work out what the problem actually is,
before accepting anybody's statement of it.

The distinction the step exists for is **problem versus proposed solution**. Users arrive
with a solution already in mind and describe that instead ("we need a bigger spreadsheet"),
so taking the request at face value builds the wrong system correctly. Recognition means
going one level up: what goes wrong today, how often, for whom, and what it costs. Only then
do you know which of the several possible solutions is worth evaluating in
[[Evaluation and Synthesis]].

It also fixes the **scope**: what is inside the system and what is outside it. The people and
systems that sit on the boundary are the actors that later show up in
[[Use Case Diagrams]].

Getting this step wrong is the worst case on the [[SDLC]] cost curve, because everything
downstream is correct work on the wrong problem, and testing will not catch it: the system
does what the specification says.
